thread:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: paging: high p99 tail latency detected on continuous-batching path in us-west-2. metric: inference.latency_p99 spiked to 2.3s across streaming routes. auto-page to #incidents

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-3789. Severity: Sev2. Affected: streaming endpoints (chat/stream) on cont-batch runtime. Notifying oncall.

maya (oncall): got the page. seeing p95 ~450ms, p99 ~2300ms, tail is where it bites. streaming stalls being reported by customer app logs.

eli: looking at scheduler metrics — queue depth for cont-batch increased, pack size median up to 48, but a big fraction of requests are tiny (len<16) mixed with some huge sequences >1024. packing amplification + mixed seqlen causing kv-cache churn.

samir: confirms: KV eviction rate up 3x last 30m. KV hits drop correlates with latency spikes. appears to be continuous batching path not traditional streaming path.

sasha (eng-sre): can we temporarily disable cont-batch packing for streaming routes? or reduce max_pack_size to limit amplification.

maya (oncall): proposing emergency mitigation: 1) reduce cont-batch max_pack_size from 64 to 16, 2) enable preemptive short-seq priority for streaming, 3) route known low-latency customers to dedicated low-latency pool (if available). anyone object?

terin (infra): reducing pack_size now on us-west-2 runtime group 'cb-prod-usw2' in staging then prod. patch config: 
```
batching.max_pack_size: 16
batching.enable_seq_priority: true
preemptive.short_seq_threshold: 32
```
Applying to node pool now.

eli: adding a shed policy for oversized sequences — heavy >2048 get routed to long-run pool. will push routing rule in 60s.

samir: pushing kv-cache pin tuning: increase per-request kv-reserve to reduce eviction thrash. small change, deploying.

ops-bot: Deploy triggered by terin: rolling config update on cb-prod-usw2 (8 nodes). ETA ~2m per node.

maya (oncall): customer impact check: Carla, can you triage CS tickets? which customers saw errors vs latency?

carla (cs): we have 3 customers reported streaming stalls: 'noteAI' with partial responses and reconnects, 'chatly' observed intermittent transcript gaps, one internal partner. I'll inform them we're mitigating and may route to low-latency fallback. prepping a customer message.

sasha (eng-sre): after first node patch: p99 fell from 2.3s -> 1.4s in that node, overall cluster p99 trending down. still above SLO. continue roll.

eli: logs show pack composition changed after max_pack_size lowered: median pack size dropped to 12, tail pack size much lower. KV eviction rate down 45%. good signal.

maya (oncall): next step: keep rolling to all nodes. if p99 doesn't drop below 700ms after full roll, we fallback to disabling cont-batch for streaming (risking cost increase).

samir: opened a short-lived feature flag to disable cont-batch on streaming: `ff/disable-contbatch-streaming`. will be ready to flip if needed.

incident-bot: Update INC-2024-3789: mitigation actions in progress.

terin (infra): roll complete across cluster. aggregate metrics: p95 360ms, p99 610ms. streaming stall reports decreased.

maya (oncall): nice. still seeing occasional p99 spikes aligned with customer 'noteAI' sessions with huge sequences (token_len > 3000).

eli: created a routing rule to send sessions with high seqlen estimates to long-run pool and disable streaming for those sessions. rule: `if seq_est > 2000 -> pool: long-run-no-stream`. deployed.

carla (cs): notified noteAI about mitigation and routing; they're ok with degraded streaming for large sessions, prefer no disconnects.

maya (oncall): final checks: logs show no new errors, latency within SLO for majority. plan: keep mitigations for 3 hours, monitor, follow up with RCA and action items: 
- shard-level batching fairness audit
- improve seqlen estimation at ingress to prevent mispacking
- automatic pack_size autoscaling based on seqlen distribution
- better telemetry on KV eviction causes

sasha (eng-sre): adding ops runbook update: emergency knob names and rollback steps.

samir: I'll own a post-incident ticket to test preemptive scheduling improvements and quantize effects.

maya (oncall): Carla to notify customers that incident is mitigated; Samir/Sasha/Terin/Maya will do RCA doc in #postmortems. low urgency follow-up for infra to consider dedicated streaming lanes.

carla (cs): customer messages sent. no escalations.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2024-3789 marked: mitigated (actions applied). Awaiting RCA.

maya (oncall): closing thread for live mitigation. leaving FF flagged to ready state for 30m then auto-unflag if stable. tagging for postmortem: @sasha @samir @eli @terin @carla
